title: Introduce territory-scoped service profiles, KMS consent mosaic, and opaque audit encoder
author: Ethan Park
description: Motivation: Customers running in multi-jurisdiction deployments need predictable enforcement for operator actions, key usage, and audit retention that respects territorial constraints. This PR implements a service-profile centric approach to RBAC v2 where operator permissions, default KMS consent strategies, and audit-encoding policies are bound to a territory identifier. Design summary: 1) Territory-scoped Service Profiles: new declarative YAML profile objects (profiles/) that capture operator role templates, allowed KMS providers per territory, and a region-pin matrix for routing. Profiles are layered at service, team and tenant levels with deterministic precedence. 2) KMS Consent Mosaic: a consent resolver that emits a signed consent assertion for KMS calls when a territory requires per-request provenance. The resolver supports multi-provider mosaics (primary + fallbacks) and annotates outgoing KMS request metadata for downstream attestors. 3) Opaque Audit Encoder: a compact, encrypted audit envelope format (v2) that attaches territorial metadata and policy fingerprints while minimizing PII in logs. Encoder supports streaming-friendly chunked envelopes and deterministic canonicalization for dedupe. Migration plan: - Add profiles to config CRD and ship a small CLI migration tool to generate profiles from existing region-pin maps. - Backfill: run audit-encoder backfill for last 90 days (configurable) using a consumer-job; non-blocking, runs in parallel. - Rollout: stage behind a feature flag territory-profiles.v1; enable in canary region, monitor audit integrity and KMS latencies. Checklist: - [x] API and CRD schema (profiles/v1) - [x] RBAC validation hooks for territory inheritance - [x] KMS consent resolver + tests - [x] Opaque audit encoder + compatibility layer (decoder) - [x] CLI migration tool and docs - [x] E2E test against dedicated and private deploys Testing and verification: unit tests for consent resolver, schema conformance checks, integration test that simulates KMS primary outage and ensures mosaic fallback is used, and audit-envelope compatibility tests against old decoder. Metrics added: rbac.profile.enforce.latency, kms.consent.signed, audit.encoder.envelope.count, audit.encoder.backfill.duration. Observability: New dashboards in Console > Security -> Territories shows per-profile policy drift alerts and KMS consent failure rates. Compatibility notes: decoders for opaque envelopes are backwards compatible; if decoding fails the system emits an obfuscated placeholder and routes to legacy audit storage for inspection. Security review summary: included threat model and KMS key access minimization; crypto review approved ephemeral signer approach. Rollout window and rollback: 48 hour progressive canary with immediate feature-flag toggle; rollback reverts profile lookup to previous global map. Related: references ENG-2142 (policy model), SEC-73 (consent cryptography), SUP-1983 for a customer support case that motivated region mosaic behavior.

release_notes: Add territory-scoped service profiles (CRD), KMS consent mosaic for multi-provider consent, and a compact encrypted audit envelope (v2). Includes migration CLI and a backfill job for historical audit data. Feature gated behind territory-profiles.v1.
